title: Private installer: add KMS config preflight validation (key ID, region, permissions) with actionable errors
creator: Vivek Kulkarni
project: Security & Compliance Foundation: KMS integration hardening + rotation docs
body:
## Context
Private customers are repeatedly failing late in install/upgrade due to KMS misconfiguration (wrong key ARN/ID, region mismatch, missing permissions, missing grants). These show up as generic decrypt failures in data-plane logs, causing long support loops.

This ticket adds *installer-side preflight checks* so we fail fast with actionable, provider-specific remediation steps, and generate an evidence-friendly validation report (useful during enterprise security reviews and audits).

Related signals:
- SUP-19341 (Private customer decrypt AccessDenied)
- SUP-19377 (KMS throttling causing elevated 5xx) – not directly fixed here, but preflight should detect obvious quota/policy pitfalls where possible
- Project initiative: “KMS integration hardening + rotation docs”

## Goal
Add a KMS validation step to the Private installer that verifies:
1) Key identifier is syntactically valid and resolvable (exists, enabled)
2) Region / location is consistent with the cluster region and configured endpoints
3) Runtime principal has minimum required permissions for envelope operations
4) Installer prints actionable errors mapped to Redwood’s KMS error taxonomy (AccessDenied, NotFound, Disabled, InvalidArn/Id, RegionMismatch, ThrottlingRisk, Timeout)

## Non-goals
- Implement new crypto primitives or change envelope scheme.
- Full runtime circuit breaker / retry policy (handled by wrapper workstream).
- End-to-end decrypt correctness tests across every data-plane component (covered elsewhere).

## Requirements / Acceptance Criteria
### Functional
- [ ] New installer command: `redwood-private validate kms` (or equivalent subcommand in existing preflight) that runs before applying manifests.
- [ ] Validation supports the primary provider patterns we document for Private:
  - AWS KMS: key ARN/alias, DescribeKey, policy/grant checks, optional STS identity confirmation
  - GCP KMS: key resource name, GetCryptoKey, IAM permission checks
  - Azure Key Vault / Managed HSM (if configured for envelope key wrapping): key URI parsing, key enabled check, permission checks
- [ ] Region mismatch detection where applicable (AWS: key region vs configured cluster region; show explicit message).
- [ ] Permission check is explicit and minimal (do not require admin permissions). Must validate:
  - ability to Encrypt/Decrypt (or Wrap/Unwrap depending on integration)
  - ability to GenerateDataKey (if used by our control plane or runtime)
  - ability to Describe/GetKey metadata
- [ ] Output includes:
  - summary (PASS/FAIL)
  - per-check result
  - remediation guidance (copy-pastable IAM snippets where appropriate)
  - correlation ID / timestamp
- [ ] Optional flag `--output validation-report.json` (or `--report`) generates a report suitable for attaching to change tickets/audits.

### UX / Error messaging
- [ ] All failures map to a canonical error category aligned with ENG-4822 and log field conventions.
- [ ] Actionable messages must mention *which principal* (role/service account/managed identity) is missing *which permission*.
- [ ] Provide “common mistakes” hints:
  - wrong key alias / typo
  - using multi-region key alias but specifying single-region ARN
  - key disabled / pending deletion
  - installer running under different principal than runtime (customer often assumes they’re the same)

### Safety
- [ ] Validation is read-only by default (no grants, no policy changes).
- [ ] If we must perform a write operation for validation, require explicit `--allow-write-checks` and describe what will be changed (preferred: avoid).

### Tests
- [ ] Unit tests for parsing + provider adapters.
- [ ] Integration tests in CI/staging using mocked provider endpoints OR controlled test keys to validate:
  - NotFound
  - AccessDenied
  - Disabled key
  - Region mismatch (AWS)

## Proposed Implementation
1) Add provider-agnostic validation interface in installer:
   - `ValidateKmsConfig(ctx, cfg) -> []CheckResult`
   - `CheckResult` includes: name, status, category, message, remediation, raw_error_code
2) Implement AWS validator:
   - Parse ARN/alias
   - Call `DescribeKey`
   - Validate `KeyState == Enabled`
   - Validate region: ARN region must equal configured region (unless documented multi-region pattern is in use; if multi-region, detect via DescribeKey output and soften guidance).
   - Permission checks:
     - Prefer `SimulatePrincipalPolicy` only if customer opts in (requires IAM permissions that are often blocked). Default should be lightweight: attempt minimal KMS API calls and interpret AccessDenied with explicit missing action.
3) Implement GCP validator:
   - Parse `projects/*/locations/*/keyRings/*/cryptoKeys/*`
   - Call `GetCryptoKey`
   - Use IAM test-permissions endpoint if available; otherwise attempt minimal operations and map errors.
4) Implement Azure validator (scoped):
   - Validate Key Vault URI and key name/version format
   - Call key “get” endpoint and check enabled
   - Attempt wrap/unwrap permission checks if feasible in a read-only manner; if not, document limitations and require runtime self-test.
5) Reporting:
   - Save report with masked sensitive identifiers (no full tokens/credentials). Key identifiers OK; redact account IDs if configured.

## Rollout Plan
- Ship behind a default-on preflight step for new installs.
- For upgrades, keep as a recommended step (installer prints “recommended” and how to run) for one release, then make it blocking in the following release after support confirms no false positives.

## Links
- GitHub: `redwood-private-installer` PR planned: pr-392-add-kms-preflight-validation-and-permission-checks
- Confluence (operator guide): Private deployment KMS integration operator guide (will need to reference this command)
- Observability: KMS dashboards/alerts PR in observability-pack (not a dependency, but validate should point to dashboards in troubleshooting output)

## Open Questions
1) Do we treat installer principal != runtime principal as an error or a warning?
   - Proposal: warning with guidance; allow explicit override `--principal runtime` when customer provides runtime identity details.
2) Azure support scope: do we validate Managed HSM differently?
   - Proposal: keep basic URL/key enabled check; rely on runtime self-test for wrap/unwrap until we have a stable adapter.

## Updates / Activity Log
- 2025-10-16 (Vivek): Filed after SUP-19341 escalations; enterprise prospects requesting “fail fast” validation.
- 2025-10-18 (Bruno): Drafted check list for AWS. Noted SimulatePrincipalPolicy is impractical for most customers; will do direct KMS calls to infer missing permissions.
- 2025-10-23 (Jordan Lee): Requested error categories align with ENG-4822 (AccessDenied vs NotAuthorized, NotFound vs InvalidArn). Also asked to include principal ARN/service account in output.
- 2025-10-29 (Kira Thompson): Docs request: command output must be copy-pastable into support tickets; include `--report` artifact so customers can attach in audits.
- 2025-11-05 (Sean Gallagher): SRE feedback: ensure preflight has a hard timeout and does not hang the installer; cap retries and print elapsed time per check.
- 2025-11-08 (Bruno): PR opened in redwood-private-installer (pr-392). Added AWS + GCP validators and JSON report output.
- 2025-11-12 (Hanae Suzuki): Security review: confirmed read-only behavior. Requested redaction rules for report and addition of correlation ID.
- 2025-11-15 (Bruno): Merged + verified in staging. Follow-up task: update operator guide to mention `validate kms` and sample remediation snippets.

## Notes for Support
If a customer reports decrypt failures, ask them to run:
- `redwood-private validate kms --report kms-validation.json`
and attach the report. The report includes categorized failures and remediation hints aligned to the KMS runbook.

## Follow-ups
- Update docs page with examples for AWS/GCP/Azure and sample output.
- Consider a runtime endpoint “KMS self-test” that can be executed post-install to catch identity differences between installer and runtime.
